title: Geoeconomic Monitor: Election Season
gist: Gavekal sees voters turning against the populist right after defeats for Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia and an ominous outlook for Republicans in the US midterms, with Spain and France as the next tests. It also warns that a resumed US-Israeli bombing campaign in Iran would send oil to new highs, and that Congress could do little to stop it even with a Democratic Senate.

insights.claim: Elections in the week to 30 Oct 2026 dealt heavy defeats to Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia, which Gavekal reads as part of a broader voter turn against the populist right.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A run of populist-right losses would reprice political-risk premia in the affected markets and challenge the assumption that the populist wave is durable.
insights.quote: This week’s elections dealt crushing blows to Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil and Aleksandar Vučić in Serbia.

insights.claim: The US midterms the following week look ominous for the Republicans, adding to the evidence that voters are turning against the populist right.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A Republican setback would shift US policy expectations, including the odds of divided government.
insights.quote: With next week’s US midterms looking ominous for the Republicans, voters appear to be turning against the populist right.

insights.claim: Whether the tide has really turned will be tested by the upcoming elections in Spain and France; Tom Miller treats these as the confirming or refuting cases for the populist-right retreat thesis.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Spain and France are the next checkpoints for whether the pattern is a trend or a run of coincidences.
insights.quote: The upcoming elections in Spain and France will show whether the tide really has turned, says Tom Miller.

insights.claim: If Israel and the US restart their bombing campaign in Iran, Tom Holland expects global oil prices to surge to new highs.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Renewed strikes on Iran are the key upside tail risk for oil, and hedging it matters ahead of the political calendar.
insights.quote: If Israel and the US restart their bombing campaign in Iran, global oil prices will surge to new highs, writes Tom Holland.

insights.claim: Netanyahu may yet cling to power in Israel, which keeps open the political incentive for renewed military action against Iran.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Netanyahu staying in office raises the chance of a restarted Iran campaign and, indirectly, of an oil spike.
insights.quote: In Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu may yet cling to power.

insights.claim: Will Denyer argues Congress can do little to stop a resumed Iran bombing campaign, even if the Democrats take the Senate in the midterms. A Democratic win would therefore not remove the oil-price tail risk.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should not treat a Democratic Senate as a hedge against renewed US military action and the resulting oil shock.
